virus.name: Virus
virus.description: Tiny particles that hijack living cells to reproduce. They are not alive on their own.
general_prevention: Avoid close contact with sick people

bacteria.name: Bacteria
bacteria.description: Single-celled living organisms. Some are harmless or helpful; others cause illness.
general_treatment: Complete the full course of medication

fungus.name: Fungus
fungus.description: Organisms like molds and yeasts. Some thrive on skin or moist surfaces and can cause infection.
general_prevention: Do not share towels or shoes
general_treatment: Oral antifungal medication for severe cases
Keep affected area dry and exposed to air

parasite.name: Parasite
parasite.description: Organisms that live on or in a host and benefit at the host's expense.
general_prevention: Use insect repellent and bed nets
general_treatment: Treat all household members if needed

pathogens.name: Influenza
pathogens.fact: Influenza spreads through respiratory droplets and can mutate every year, which is why a new flu vaccine is made each season.
treatment: Antiviral medication like oseltamivir if prescribed early

pathogens.name: SARS-CoV-2 (COVID-19)
pathogens.fact: SARS-CoV-2 spreads mainly through airborne droplets and aerosols in poorly ventilated spaces.
prevention: Well-fitted mask indoors when cases are high
Good ventilation and distance from sick people
treatment: Monitor oxygen and seek care if breathing worsens

pathogens.name: Norovirus
pathogens.fact: Norovirus is extremely contagious and causes sudden vomiting and diarrhea. Hand sanitizer alone does not kill it well.
prevention: Wash hands with soap and water (not just sanitizer)
Do not prepare food when sick
treatment: Seek care if dehydration is severe

pathogens.name: Strep Throat (Streptococcus)
pathogens.fact: Strep throat is caused by group A Streptococcus and can lead to rheumatic fever if untreated.
prevention: Do not share cups or utensils
treatment: Antibiotics such as penicillin or amoxicillin

pathogens.name: E. coli (pathogenic strains)
pathogens.fact: Harmful strains of E. coli often come from undercooked ground beef, raw produce, or contaminated water.
prevention: Cook ground beef to 160 degrees F
treatment: Most cases resolve on their own; some antibiotics can make certain strains worse, so follow a doctor's guidance

pathogens.name: Tuberculosis (TB)
pathogens.fact: TB is caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis and spreads through the air from prolonged close contact.
prevention: Screening and treatment of latent TB
treatment: Long course of multiple antibiotics for 6 or more months
Directly observed therapy to ensure completion

pathogens.name: Athlete's Foot (Tinea pedis)
pathogens.fact: Athlete's foot thrives in warm, damp environments like sweaty shoes and locker-room floors.
treatment: Keep feet dry and aired out

pathogens.name: Ringworm (Tinea corporis)
pathogens.fact: Ringworm is not a worm; it is a fungal infection that forms a ring-shaped rash on the skin.
prevention: Do not share towels or clothes
Treat pets that show bald patches
treatment: Topical antifungal cream for 2 to 4 weeks

pathogens.name: Candidiasis (Yeast Infection)
pathogens.fact: Candida yeast naturally lives on the body but overgrows when the balance is disrupted by antibiotics, moisture, or illness.
prevention: Keep skin folds clean and dry
treatment: Treat underlying causes such as uncontrolled diabetes

pathogens.name: Malaria
pathogens.fact: Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites carried by Anopheles mosquitoes. It kills hundreds of thousands of people each year.
treatment: Antimalarial drugs such as artemisinin-based combination therapy
Test and treat household members if needed

pathogens.name: Giardiasis
pathogens.fact: Giardia is a microscopic parasite that spreads through contaminated water, even in clear mountain streams.
prevention: Wash hands after using the toilet and before eating
Avoid swallowing lake or pool water
treatment: Antiparasitic medication like metronidazole or tinidazole

pathogens.name: Tapeworm
pathogens.fact: Tapeworms can be picked up from undercooked pork, beef, or fish and can live in the intestines for years.
prevention: Cook meat to a safe internal temperature
Freeze fish before eating raw preparations
treatment: Treat household members and pets if exposed

quiz.q: A patient has a bacterial infection. Which treatment is most appropriate?
quiz.explain: Bacterial infections are treated with antibiotics. It is important to finish the full course.

quiz.q: Which pathogen type is NOT alive on its own and must infect a host cell to reproduce?
quiz.explain: Viruses are not alive on their own. They hijack host cells to make more copies of themselves.

quiz.q: A child has ringworm on their arm. What is the best treatment?
quiz.explain: Ringworm is a fungal infection, not a worm. It is treated with antifungal cream.

quiz.q: Which of these is the BEST prevention for the seasonal flu?
quiz.explain: The annual flu vaccine is updated every year to match circulating strains and is the most effective prevention.
Malaria is caused by Plasmodium parasites carried by Anopheles mosquitoes. Bed nets and repellent help prevent it.

quiz.q: Which treatment helps most for viral gastroenteritis like norovirus?
quiz.explain: Antibiotics do not kill viruses. Fluids, rest, and careful hygiene are the main treatments.

quiz.q: What is the single most effective everyday action to prevent many infections?
choices: Washing hands with soap and water
quiz.explain: Hand washing with soap and water breaks the chain of transmission for many bacteria, viruses, and parasites.
TB is a bacterial infection that requires a long course of multiple antibiotics.

quiz.q: The best way to prevent giardiasis while hiking is to:
choices: Boil or filter water before drinking
quiz.explain: Giardia parasites can live in clear water. Boiling or filtering makes water safe.

quiz.q: A patient finishes feeling better after 3 days of a 10-day antibiotic course. They should:
choices: Save the rest for next time
Double the dose to speed recovery
quiz.explain: Stopping antibiotics early can leave surviving bacteria that develop resistance. Always finish the course.

quiz.q: Which is a good way to prevent athlete's foot?
choices: Dry feet well and wear sandals in locker rooms
quiz.explain: Fungi love warm, damp feet. Drying well and avoiding barefoot contact in locker rooms helps.

quiz.q: Which statement about vaccines is TRUE?
choices: They cure infections after you get them
They train your immune system to recognize pathogens
quiz.explain: Vaccines teach the immune system to recognize a pathogen so it can respond quickly if exposed later.

quiz.q: Quarantine (separating sick people) is most useful for stopping:
choices: Airborne viruses like influenza and COVID-19
quiz.explain: Isolating sick people cuts the chain of transmission for airborne respiratory viruses.

quiz.q: Which pathogen category includes yeast infections like candidiasis?
quiz.explain: Candida is a yeast, which is a type of fungus. It is treated with antifungal medication.

quiz.q: To prevent E. coli from ground beef, you should:
choices: Eat it raw for better nutrients
quiz.explain: Cooking ground beef to 160 degrees F kills harmful E. coli strains.

quiz.q: Which of these does NOT help prevent the spread of respiratory viruses?
quiz.explain: Sharing cups directly spreads droplets. The other actions all reduce transmission.

quiz.q: A tapeworm infection is usually treated with:
choices: A single antiparasitic dose like praziquantel
quiz.explain: Tapeworms respond to a targeted antiparasitic drug. Cooking meat thoroughly prevents infection.

quiz.q: Which group of diseases is usually treated with antibiotics?
quiz.explain: Strep throat and TB are bacterial and respond to antibiotics. Viruses, fungi, and parasites need different treatments.
